clue.text: Take last of harness to the tack room, opposite number 14

indicators.note: last of picks the final letter of the word harness that follows it

parts.note: a tack is a small nail
room in the sense of space to move

explanation.surface: A stable hand is told to carry the remaining harness to the tack room across from stall fourteen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last of' takes the final letter of harness. 'Opposite number 14' is not an address: it points to the answer at 14 down, a brisk military step, and asks for its contrary, a very slow rate of progress.
explanation.definitionFit: The entry at 14 is a brisk walking rate, and this idiom for extreme slowness is its antonym.

clue.text: Rifle fire

definitions.meaning: to rifle is to plunder or ransack a place
to fire someone is to dismiss them from a job

explanation.definitionFit: Two verb senses of one word: to plunder a town, and to dismiss an employee.

clue.text: Greed shown by girl over food

indicators.note: in a down clue, over places the name above the food in the grid

parts.note: Ava is a girl's name
rice is a staple food

explanation.surface: A girl shows her greediness when presented with a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' works because this is a down entry: the girl's name sits on top of the food.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: an insatiable desire for wealth or gain, one of the deadly sins.

clue.text: In a manner of speaking, some tall soldiers?

definitions.text: In a manner of speaking, some
definitions.note: said aloud, some is sum, an arithmetic problem, which is what the answer is

parts.note: a tall person can be described as long, as in long-legged
a division is a large army unit

explanation.surface: Somebody loosely describes a group of troops who happen to be unusually tall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a manner of speaking' is not a shrug: it asks you to say 'some' out loud, giving 'sum', a piece of arithmetic. The question mark excuses the whimsical picture of lanky troops.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoken, 'some' gives 'sum', and this schoolroom method of dividing big numbers is an example of an arithmetic sum.

clue.text: Brochure showing each year the rate allowed

parts.note: PA is the abbreviation of per annum, each year
MPH, miles per hour, is a rate of speed
let means allowed, as in they let him go

explanation.surface: A leaflet sets out the permitted annual interest rate.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a small printed booklet or leaflet giving information.

clue.text: Setting contract at the start, having two top cards

indicators.note: at the start picks the opening letter of the word contract before it

parts.note: A is the ace, the highest card in a suit
the king is the next highest card in a suit

explanation.surface: A bridge player fixes the contract early while holding the ace and king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at the start' takes the first letter of contract. The surface is a bridge table, but 'Setting' means hardening into a solid crust, as mud does.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym in the sense of hardening: mud forming a crust is doing both.

clue.text: Something I ran into on the way back

indicators.note: on the way back tells you the word for ran into is written backwards

parts.note: to run into someone is to meet them, so ran into is met

explanation.surface: A traveller recalls an obstacle struck during the return journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ran into' suggests a collision, but it means encountered; 'on the way back' turns that word round to give TEM.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose synonym: an article or individual thing on a list.

clue.text: Plant grass to produce chaff

parts.note: tea is a plant grown for its leaves
to grass is British slang for informing on someone, as is to sing

explanation.surface: A farmer sows grass seed and ends up with husks.
explanation.walkthrough: To grass is British slang for informing to the police, just as a criminal who sings does. 'Chaff' is not husks here but good-natured banter.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym as a noun: light-hearted mockery or banter.

clue.text: Girl near me is naughty. — she pretends to be out of work

definitions.text: she pretends to be out of work

indicators.note: naughty means badly behaved, so the letters before it are out of their proper order

explanation.surface: A badly behaved girl nearby is faking unemployment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'naughty' rearranges the three words before it. The definition is gently twisted: she feigns illness so as to be off work.
explanation.definitionFit: A description of a shirker who fakes illness to avoid her duties.

clue.text: Constrains ass to behave like an addict

parts.note: to chain something is to constrain it, so constrains is chains
moke is British slang for a donkey

explanation.surface: Someone forces a donkey into the habits of a junkie.
explanation.walkthrough: MOKE is old British slang for a donkey, the ass of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A description: lighting one cigarette from the last is nicotine dependence in action.

clue.text: Security man has no heart

indicators.note: has no heart tells you to drop the middle letter of the name

parts.note: Basil is a man's name

explanation.surface: A guard is a pitiless fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has no heart' removes the central S of BASIL.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym in law: money pledged to guarantee a defendant's return to court.

clue.text: Apaches rob us — set in motion legal procedure

indicators.note: set in motion means the letters before it are stirred into movement and rearranged

explanation.surface: After a raid by Apaches, the victims start court proceedings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set in motion' rearranges the three opening words; in the surface it merely starts the lawsuit.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: the writ requiring a detained person to be brought before a court.

clue.text: Song told a story

definitions.meaning: a German art song for voice and piano, as written by Schubert
to tell a story is a euphemism for saying something untrue

explanation.definitionFit: The German word for an art song is spelt the same as the past tense of telling an untruth.

clue.text: Liszt, for example, executed a piece of music with the ultimate in élan

parts.note: a person executed on the gallows was hung
an aria is a solo song in an opera

indicators.note: the ultimate in picks the final letter of the word élan after it

explanation.surface: Liszt, say, performed a composition with supreme flair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the ultimate in' takes the last letter of élan. 'executed' looks like performing music but means put to death.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Liszt was born in Hungary, so he is an example of this nationality.

clue.text: Allegro piece of music in order for military band

parts.note: allegro is the musical direction for a fast tempo
a march is a piece of music written for marching

explanation.surface: A lively composition is on the programme for an army band.
explanation.definitionFit: A drill command telling a body of troops to step off at a brisk rate.

clue.text: A European to compete in a bit of bowling? It's resented by nobody

parts.note: un is the French word for a

indicators.note: in puts the word for compete inside the bowling term

parts.note: an end is one stage of play in a game of bowls
to vie is to compete

explanation.surface: A continental player enters a bowls match, and no one minds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A European' is the article as a Frenchman says it, and 'in' is the container signal. In the British game of bowls an end is one passage of play in a single direction; the surface hints at cricket instead.
explanation.definitionFit: A description: nobody begrudges or covets something of this kind.

clue.text: Hunt the blackbird

parts.note: the first half, black, is abbreviated B as on pencils
the second half, bird, is an eagle, a bird of prey

explanation.surface: Someone goes looking for a blackbird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blackbird' must be split in two: black, then bird. The definition is a verb meaning to go hunting hares on foot with small hounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A verb for one kind of hunting: following a pack of small hounds after hares.

clue.text: Leave breathless and in pain a novice trailing the race

indicators.note: in puts the race and the novice inside the word for pain

parts.note: a throe is a violent pang of pain

indicators.note: trailing places the novice's letter after the race

parts.note: the TT is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle race on the Isle of Man
L is the letter on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A beginner lagging behind the field is left gasping and hurting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal and 'trailing' fixes the order of the two pieces inside. The race is a British motorcycle event on the Isle of Man, and a British learner driver displays a plate with one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to choke someone, stopping their air.

clue.text: Sweep into exams — how rude!

indicators.note: into puts the rowing word inside the exams

parts.note: CSE, the Certificate of Secondary Education, was a set of British school exams
a sweep is a long oar used to row or steer a boat

explanation.surface: Someone barges into the exam hall with no manners at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweep' looks like a verb of grand entrance but is a noun, a long rowing blade; 'into' is the container signal. The exams are ones British sixteen-year-olds sat until the 1980s.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: vulgar or crude in manner.

clue.text: Reduce the length of a spanner.

parts.note: a bridge spans a river, so it is whimsically a spanner

explanation.surface: A mechanic shortens a wrench.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spanner' is not the British word for a wrench here but something that spans a gap.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to shorten a book or text.

clue.text: Dangerous gas seepage — gas engineers at the outset within call

indicators.note: within puts the three initial letters inside the word for call

parts.note: to call someone is to phone them

indicators.note: at the outset picks the opening letters of seepage, gas and engineers

explanation.surface: A hazardous gas leak is reported, with gas engineers on call from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at the outset' takes the first letters of seepage, the second gas and engineers; 'within' puts those three inside PHONE.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a poisonous gas used as a chemical weapon in the First World War.

clue.text: Taken out of context, ,remember, it's immoderate

indicators.note: Taken out of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A remark seems excessive once quoted without its background.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: something far beyond the reasonable or ordinary.

clue.text: Palm tree acting as a protective covering

parts.note: coco is a name for the coconut palm
an actor who is acting is on, meaning on stage

explanation.surface: A palm tree serves as shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: the silk case a caterpillar spins around itself.

clue.text: Merchant backing to push business game

indicators.note: backing tells you the word for push is written backwards

parts.note: to ram is to push with force
Co is the abbreviation of company, a business
polo is a game played on horseback

explanation.surface: A trader offers support to promote a commercial venture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns RAM into MAR. The merchant is a named one: the Venetian trader who travelled to China.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: the Venetian trader famous for his travels to the court of Kublai Khan.

clue.text: Loyalty's oddly lacking in grasses

indicators.note: oddly lacking drops the odd-numbered letters of Loyalty's, leaving the even ones

explanation.surface: Faithfulness is strangely absent among police informers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly lacking' removes the odd letters. 'grasses' is British slang for informers in the surface, but here it is the plain cereal plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Examples: cereal plants belonging to the grass family.

clue.text: Look noble

definitions.meaning: to look closely or with difficulty, as through a fog
a noble as a noun: a lord such as a duke or an earl

explanation.definitionFit: One word is both a verb for gazing hard and a noun for a member of the aristocracy.

clue.text: Pestered to wear no cap

indicators.note: no cap means the word for wear loses its top, its first letter

parts.note: to wear away is to erode

explanation.surface: Someone is nagged into going bareheaded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no cap' removes the first letter E of ERODE.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to ride someone is to harass or nag them, and this is its past tense.

clue.text: As a spokesperson, I come up with the evasions

indicators.note: evasions are dodges and shifts, so the letters of the words before it shift about

explanation.surface: A press officer admits to being the one who invents the dodges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'evasions' rearranges 'I come up' and 'the'; 'with' only joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a person who speaks on behalf of another or of an organisation.

clue.text: Went quickly and fell noisily

indicators.note: noisily tells you the word for fell is heard rather than read

parts.note: a fell is an animal's skin or hide

explanation.surface: Somebody rushed off and took a loud tumble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fell' is not a tumble but an old noun for an animal's pelt; 'noisily' asks for that word as it is said.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: an archaic past tense meaning hastened.

clue.text: Resent rude constituents, but don't turn away

indicators.note: constituents are component parts, so the component letters of the two words before it are used to build something new

explanation.surface: An MP is advised to dislike ill-mannered voters but not to shun them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'constituents' rearranges the letters of the first two words. The definition is wry: a car doing this turns less sharply than the driver steers.
explanation.definitionFit: A description: a car doing this fails to turn as sharply as the wheel asks.
